question: Does the 2018 PNR South Commuter EIS provide station-resolved fish evidence for the San Juan River in Calamba?

sourceReviewed.citation: Department of Transportation. (2018, May). Environmental Impact Statement for the PNR South Commuter (North South Railway Project (NSRP) – South Line (Commuter)), Volume I: Main Report (Draft Final Report). Prepared by GEOSPHERE Technologies, Inc.
sourceReviewed.access: Full PDF text reviewed from the DENR EMB EIA portal. No local PDF or figure was copied into the repository.
sections: Table 3.2.15: Coordinates and Elevation of Surveyed Stations
Paragraphs 728-729 and Table 3.2.19: Fish and Other Aquatic Animals Reportedly Caught at Five Stations
Paragraph 732: project-impact discussion referencing multiple named sites

fieldSurvey.scope: Freshwater ecology sampling at 13 stations along the project alignment
fieldSurvey.ecologySamplingDates: February 8-9, 2018; individual station dates are listed in Table 3.2.15
fieldSurvey.fishMethod: Paragraph 713 states that locals were interviewed about river use and fish/other aquatic animals caught in the area. The report does not state that the fish in Table 3.2.19 were collected, identified, or vouchered by the ecology team.

fishTable.tableTitle: Fish and Other Aquatic Animals Reportedly Caught at Five (5) Stations
fishTable.evidenceType: local-informant-reported-catch; no specimen or capture-date confirmation

taxonomicCrosscheck.citation: Chavez, J. M., de la Paz, R. M., Manohar, S. K., Pagulayan, R. C., & Carandang VI, J. R. (2006). New Philippine record of South American sailfin catfishes (Pisces: Loricariidae). Zootaxa, 1109(1), 57-68. https://doi.org/10.11646/zootaxa.1109.1.6
taxonomicCrosscheck.reviewedFinding: The peer-reviewed study examined 193 specimens from five Laguna de Bay-basin sites and identified Pterygoplichthys disjunctivus and P. pardalis. It states that its results do not dispel local reports of Hypostomus plecostomus, while concluding that the janitor fish commonly encountered in the sampled basin were Pterygoplichthys.
taxonomicCrosscheck.geographicLimit: The study is related basin-level evidence, not a San Juan River SW7 voucher or a verified crosswalk to the EIS catch reports.
taxonomicCrosscheck.decision: Do not resolve the EIS's interview-reported Hypostomus plecostomus label to either Pterygoplichthys species, or treat it as proof of Hypostomus plecostomus, without a San Juan specimen, diagnostic image, sequence, or independently validated record.
taxonomicCrosscheck.reuse: The publisher PDF identifies Magnolia Press copyright; no open reuse license was identified. Do not reproduce article photos, figures, tables, or text.

stationCrosswalk.ecologySeries: Table 3.2.15 assigns freshwater-ecology SW7 to San Juan River, Calamba City; Table 3.2.19 uses SW7 and lists locally reported catches.
stationCrosswalk.waterQualitySeries: The separate 14-station water-quality series labels San Juan River SW8, while its SW7 is San Cristobal River. Paragraph 732 uses WSS7/WSS8 names consistent with this alternate series.
stationCrosswalk.internalConflict: Paragraph 729 says species richness was highest at SW7, then SW8 and SW12, but Table 3.2.19 has no SW8 row. Its five table rows are SW2, SW6, SW7, SW9, and SW12. Preserve this narrative/table mismatch; do not shift species rows to repair it.
stationCrosswalk.decision: The explicit Table 3.2.15 ecology-site description and Table 3.2.19 SW7 row form a provisional name-level station crosswalk for the reported catch. The narrative's station numbering and catch timing remain unresolved.

validationNeeded: The 2006 Laguna de Bay-basin taxonomic study is cross-checked; it does not resolve the EIS's unvouchered San Juan interview label to a species.
Keep Clarias sp., Channa sp., and Arius at genus level; do not infer a species from local names.
The report's Oreochromis niloticus identification is a source-reported name only; source-specific specimen confirmation is absent.
Check item-specific reuse terms before displaying derived rows or reproducing the table/photos in Bangwit.
taxonomyAndRights.imageDecision: The report photographs show people fishing, not identifiable fish vouchers. No image was copied or used to validate the Bangwit photo registry.

limits: The cover identifies this as a May 2018 Draft Final Report; it is not a comprehensive San Juan River checklist.
The ecology station coordinate marks a sampled station, not the reported fish capture locations or a whole-river distribution point.
The interviewed catches have no separate dates, effort, independent fish identification, voucher numbers, or sequence records in the reviewed passages.
A separate BatStateU-hosted Table 31 remains only an indexed retrieval lead. Its relationship, if any, to this EIS has not been established; their table contents must not be merged.
No safety, legal catchability, present-day presence, salinity class, or whole-river geometry conclusion follows from this EIS review.
nextAction: Search for independently documented San Juan River vouchers or location-dated fish observations and resolve item-specific reuse terms before any public projection; keep the community-reported list research-only meanwhile.
